purpose: Add literature-driven, orthogonal candidate mechanisms without performance selection or parameter search.

candidates.name: Institutional Demand × Accrual State
candidates.hypothesis: Publicly disclosed changes in 13F institutional ownership may carry different forward information when combined with a fixed accrual-intensity state derived from the latest PIT-valid SEC XBRL filing.
candidates.construction: Quarter-over-quarter disclosed institutional ownership change × latest publicly available accrual intensity; both components are frozen at their own EDGAR acceptance timestamps and aligned to the next eligible session.
literature_basis: Short-term institutional trading and return predictability in high-accrual stocks (2026)
Which investors drive anomaly returns and how? (2026)

candidates.name: Institutional Demand × Fundamental-Change Surprise
candidates.hypothesis: Institutional ownership changes may interact with the direction of newly public fundamental changes, creating a distinct demand-information transmission state.
candidates.construction: PIT quarterly 13F ownership change combined with a fixed signed change in a predeclared SEC XBRL fundamental measure; use only facts whose filing acceptance timestamp precedes the decision timestamp.
literature_basis: Which investors drive anomaly returns and how? (2026)
Realized, expected and unexpected returns in asset pricing tests (2026)

candidates.name: Short-Flow Triangulation State
candidates.hypothesis: Settlement pressure, reported short interest and daily short-sale volume represent different clocks of the same crowding process; their agreement/disagreement can be treated as an explicit state rather than as interchangeable proxies.
candidates.construction: Combine latest published SEC FTD state, FINRA short-interest state and FINRA Reg SHO daily short-sale-volume state using only source values already public at the decision timestamp; no post-hoc weighting.
sources: FINRA Reg SHO daily short-sale volume
literature_basis: Research OS source lattice; public short-flow convergence path

candidates.name: Filing Arrival Density × Delayed Price Response
candidates.hypothesis: Clusters of newly public SEC filings may contain information even when the immediate price reaction is small, creating a measurable event-arrival/response state.
candidates.construction: For each issuer, fixed-count recent accepted filings over a predeclared business-day window form an arrival-density state; compare with a predeclared next-session price response using only information public by the cutoff.
candidates.next_gate: synthetic event-order mutation tests + archive coverage
literature_basis: SEC information-flow research frontier; Q100/Q096 feasibility findings

candidates.name: Treasury Auction Demand Shock
candidates.hypothesis: Unexpected strength or weakness in Treasury auction demand may propagate into equity risk-taking through rates/liquidity conditions.
candidates.construction: Use fixed Treasury auction-result fields available at publication time (for example, bid-to-cover and accepted yield versus pre-auction reference) as a next-session cross-asset state; no forecast model or parameter fitting.
sources: U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data auction dataset

candidates.name: Cross-Family Consensus Reliability State
candidates.hypothesis: Agreement across genuinely distinct, fixed research families may contain a reliability state that is more informative than any one signal alone.
candidates.construction: Use only a predeclared fixed set of frozen family outputs; derive a deterministic agreement/reliability state from cross-family sign agreement and dispersion without fitting weights or selecting the best family.
literature_basis: Can the Anomaly Zoo Speak with One Voice? Consensus, Reliability, and Expected Returns (2026)

notes: These mechanisms are research hypotheses, not project evidence.
No candidate is ranked or preferred.
No performance, holdout selection, parameter search, promotion or live execution is authorized.
Candidates may be rejected at the data/PIT stage without performance testing.
